Use in project collections and recent-project sections. The name is the primary navigation action.

Show a recognisable project name, a short location or scope, room count and a concise progress summary.

## Do not
Put unrelated nested click targets inside a single interactive card. Keep destructive project actions in the project menu.

components.name: Homeowner
components.description: Plans a home renovation, compares alternatives and keeps the work, budget and evidence together.
components.responsibility: Makes renovation decisions and maintains the project information that the application presents.
components.documentation:
## Primary job
Understand what should change in my home, what the work involves and what I can afford.

## Context
Uses a familiar notes workspace. Precision is available on demand; everyday vocabulary comes first.

This is a C4 person, not a software component.

components.responsibility: Keep the homeowner’s existing home, planned changes and delivery work understandable in one local project.
components.documentation:
## Scope
Property and project planning, a spatial editor, an asset catalogue and cost planning.

## Boundary
The model includes the plugin application and its project-data store. Obsidian provides the host workspace and file APIs.

## Product principle
A homeowner workspace with direct manipulation and numeric precision when needed.

The plugin integrates through Obsidian’s public APIs. The host is outside the Renovation Planner system boundary.

Workspace views, commands, settings and vault operations. Host theme variables determine the interface appearance.

Runs inside the Obsidian host process. Its components are logical implementation boundaries, not independently deployed services.

Represents the Renovation Planner project files, not the entire Obsidian vault.

## Durability
Updates pass through the repository adapter and the host Vault API. Read errors, conflicting edits and invalid records must remain visible.

## Portability
A project export includes metadata, references and a manifest.

components.description: Maintains spatial selection, plan commands and the relationship between rooms, objects and project entities.
components.responsibility: Execute reversible plan operations while separating world coordinates, viewport state and persistent project data.

## Editing model
Selection is the default. Pan and zoom affect the viewport. Existing, Planned and Work are separate planning layers.

## Commands
Create room, move object, change dimensions, select entity and change active layer.

## Precision
The geometry policy validates dimensions and derives measurements. The interface requests commands rather than mutating domain objects directly.

This record describes an implementation module beneath the Spatial plan editor component.

Accept finite coordinates in metres. Reject self-intersections and zero-area polygons. Return explicit validation results.

## Verification
Use meaningful examples for concave rooms, edge intersections and unit conversion boundaries.

components.description: A compact project summary that helps a homeowner recognise a renovation and pick up where they left off.
components.responsibility: Display project identity, progress and budget, and emit an explicit request to open the selected project.

## When to use
Use in project collections and recent-project sections. The name is the primary navigation action.

## Content
Show a recognisable project name, a short location or scope, room count and a concise progress summary.

## Behavior
The open action emits the stable project ID. Secondary actions do not trigger navigation.

## Do not
Put unrelated nested click targets inside a single interactive card. Keep destructive project actions in the project menu.

## Example revision
Version 1.3.0 adds the compact presentation without changing the open event.
